steps.message:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station T-13 (survey area T). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1340.2 | 1.08 | 1.08
2 | 2148.3 | 1.38 | 2.46
3 | 5322.7 | 1.26 | 3.72
4 | 18475.7 | 0.33 | 4.05
5 | 19320.3 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as AKH-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Reference note: Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station: T-13
Curve type: A (recalculated from the resistivity sequence — 1340.2 < 2148.3 < 5322.7 < 18475.7 < 19320.3 gives AAA for the three triplets, which reduces to A; the file's "AKH" label does not match the logged resistivities and should be corrected)
Aquifer depth: approximately 1.08–3.72 m (the moderate-resistivity zone in layers 2–3, interpreted as weathered/fractured material overlying competent bedrock)
Recommendation: Focus drilling and screen placement within the 1–3.7 m interval, as resistivities above 18,000 ohm-m below ~4.05 m indicate massive, largely unfractured bedrock with low water-yield potential; verify with drill cuttings since the curve type on file was mislabeled and should be re-checked against raw field data.
